code.originalText: Four-week follow-up: results and MRI review, diagnosis disclosure, and behavioral neurology consultation

text.paragraph: Four-week follow-up: results and MRI, diagnosis, and behavioral neurology consultation the same day. [S]

Mr. Olmsted is a 73-year-old man evaluated four weeks ago for about two years of worsening memory, who returns with his caregiver for his results and is seen by behavioral neurology on the same day. Since the first visit he has stopped the glass of wine with dinner. He still repeats questions, loses track of letters and plans, and needs reminders for appointments; his caregiver now handles his medicines and bill paying. He has driven only short familiar routes, and once took a wrong turn near home this month. He sleeps well, has no hallucinations, acting out of dreams, falls, or urinary problems, and his mood is low at times when he thinks about leaving his work. The blood tests at the first visit were normal, and the brain MRI two weeks ago showed generalized and mild medial temporal atrophy with minor small-vessel change, without a stroke, tumor, or fluid build-up. [S]

list.item:
Mild dementia, type undetermined (F03.A0). Behavioral neurology confirms mild dementia (CDR 1), with IADL loss and intact basic ADL. No reversible cause was found on the blood tests, and the MRI shows no stroke, tumor, or hydrocephalus. The pattern of amnestic decline with executive difficulty and mild medial temporal atrophy fits Alzheimer's disease, but the MRI findings are not specific and no biomarker has been done, so the type remains undetermined. The diagnosis was shared with him and his caregiver, and he asked that it be explained to him plainly. [S]
Start donepezil 5 mg each morning, as neurology advises, and increase to 10 mg at the three-month visit if tolerated.
Stop driving now, as neurology advises; he agreed.
Avoid over-the-counter sleep aids, antihistamines such as diphenhydramine, and bladder or stomach medicines with anticholinergic effects.
Caregiver information on the Alzheimer's Association helpline and education programs.
Advance care planning at the three-month visit, while he can take full part.

text.paragraph: Guideline basis: Practice parameter: diagnosis of dementia (an evidence-based review). Report of the Quality Standards Subcommittee of the American Academy of Neurology (2001); Practice parameter update: evaluation and management of driving risk in dementia: report of the Quality Standards Subcommittee of the American Academy of Neurology (2010); Alzheimer's Association clinical practice guideline for the Diagnostic Evaluation, Testing, Counseling, and Disclosure of Suspected Alzheimer's Disease and Related Disorders (DETeCD-ADRD): Executive summary of recommendations for primary care (2025); The Alzheimer's Association clinical practice guideline for the Diagnostic Evaluation, Testing, Counseling, and Disclosure of Suspected Alzheimer's Disease and Related Disorders (DETeCD-ADRD): Executive summary of recommendations for specialty care (2025); American Geriatrics Society 2023 updated AGS Beers Criteria for potentially inappropriate medication use in older adults (2023); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, Non-Alzheimer's dementia and Alzheimer's disease monographs (2026)

Follow-up: Three-month dementia review with the donepezil dose decision, the Zarit Burden Interview, and advance care planning. Next scheduled visit 1895-08-04: three-month dementia review: donepezil, safety plan, caregiver burden, and advance care planning. [S]
